title: Derivatives, The Power Rule & Tangent Lines
outcomes: Differentiate polynomials exactly using the power rule and linearity, and evaluate f'(x_0) at a given point.
Construct the tangent line y = f(x_0) + f'(x_0)(x - x_0) to a curve and determine its exact y-intercept B.
Find exact rational critical points x where a quadratic curve has a horizontal tangent line f'(x) = 0.

sections.intuition: A secant line through (x₀, f(x₀)) and (x₀ + h, f(x₀ + h)) measures the average rate of change over an interval of width h. As h → 0, the secant line pivots into the tangent line at x₀, and its limiting slope is the derivative f'(x₀). For any power x^n, expanding (x + h)^n by the Binomial Theorem shows that (x + h)^n - x^n = n x^(n-1) h + (higher powers of h); dividing by h and taking h → 0 proves the power rule d/dx(x^n) = n x^(n-1).
sections.formal_definition:
1. Difference Quotient Definition: f'(x) = lim_{h→0} [f(x + h) - f(x)] / h.
2. Power Rule & Linearity: For integers n ≥ 1 and constants c, d/dx(x^n) = n x^(n-1) and d/dx(c) = 0. Thus for f(x) = ax³ + bx² + cx + d, f'(x) = 3ax² + 2bx + c.
3. Tangent Line at x = x₀: The line tangent to y = f(x) at (x₀, f(x₀)) has slope m = f'(x₀) and equation y = f'(x₀)(x - x₀) + f(x₀), with y-intercept B = f(x₀) - f'(x₀)x₀.
4. Stationary / Critical Points: A differentiable function has a horizontal tangent at x if and only if f'(x) = 0.
sections.worked_example:
Find the equation and y-intercept B of the line tangent to f(x) = 2x² + 3x + 5 at x₀ = 2.
1. Evaluate the point on the curve: y₀ = f(2) = 2(4) + 3(2) + 5 = 19.
2. Differentiate using the power rule: f'(x) = 4x + 3.
3. Evaluate the tangent slope at x₀ = 2: m = f'(2) = 4(2) + 3 = 11.
4. Find the y-intercept B: y = 11(x - 2) + 19 = 11x - 3, so B = -3.
common_misconceptions: Keeping the constant term d when differentiating a polynomial (the derivative of a constant is 0).
Confusing the tangent slope f'(x₀) with the tangent y-intercept B = f(x₀) - f'(x₀)x₀.
Forgetting the factor of 2 when differentiating ax² to find a critical point (writing ax - b = 0 instead of 2ax - b = 0).
